newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian lending rate slides to 10.8.
newsitem.headline: Croatian lending rate slides to 10.8.

text.p: The Croatian average lending rate slid to 10.8 percent on Thursday from 11.9 percent previously amid weaker demand for kuna, particularly for term loans, dealers said.
The day's trade totalled 50.1 million kuna, leaving another 19.9 million in supply. Banks also slightly increased their Lombard borrowing from the central bank to 53.4 million kuna.
The interbank call money rate ended at a weighted 10.4 percent as some lenders cut quotes, down from 10.9 percent.
Term rates ranged from 9.0 percent for one-week to 16 percent for one-month deals.
Insurers prolonged ten-day loans at 9.0 percent, while 11-day and two-week funds were granted at 12 percent.

With Friday a national holiday, the central bank calculated its kuna mid-rates for Saturday and next Monday firmer at 6.0822 against the dollar and at 3.5677 against the mark. -- Sandra Kalogjera, Zagreb Newsroom 385-1-4557075
